clue.text: What petty thief is prone to? Some tack

definitions.text: What petty thief is prone to?
definitions.meaning: a petty thief tends to snaffle (pinch) bits, small items, rather than anything big
mouthpieces on a horse's bridle, part of its tack

explanation.surface: A riddle about a small-time thief's habits, followed by a nod to horse riding.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAFFLE is informal British for pinch or steal; tack is a horse's riding gear (saddle, bridle, bits).
explanation.definitionFit: Snaffle bits are a common type of bridle mouthpiece, so they are examples of horse gear.

clue.text: Hopping mad?

parts.note: hopping mad means furious; a cross rabbit, a hopper, would be in a bad mood

explanation.surface: A two-word description of someone furious, or of an animal that hops.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a disgruntled person is pictured literally as a rabbit that is angry, since rabbits hop.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for someone displeased or annoyed, which is what being furious amounts to.

clue.text: Smooth pad

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means level, without bumps
pad is slang for one's home, especially an apartment

explanation.definitionFit: Level surfaces lack bumps, and an apartment is someone's living quarters, informally a pad.

clue.text: One of five N American Greats maybe, Clark Gable's weird

definitions.text: One of five N American Greats maybe

parts.note: Clark Gable was called the King of Hollywood: LA K, Los Angeles plus K for king
eerie means weird or uncanny

explanation.surface: A boast that the film star was strange enough to rank among the greats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greats' looks like great actors but means the Great Lakes. Clark Gable, 'the King of Hollywood', is rendered as LA (Los Angeles, home of Hollywood) plus K (king).
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Erie is one of the five Great Lakes on the US–Canada border, hence an example of them.

clue.text: Breaking law stranded king?

parts.note: the answer read as wordplay puts R (rex, king) in a word for strand or shore, a king beached, that is stranded

explanation.surface: A query whether a monarch left stranded counts as a breach of the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the answer is R (rex, king) placed within BEACH, a shore: a king beached, which is to say stranded.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is an infringement of a rule or law, so breaking the law is committing one.

clue.text: A fixture at Old Trafford possibly, check striker in box?

definitions.text: A fixture at Old Trafford possibly

parts.note: to test is to check
a match is struck to light it and comes in a matchbox

explanation.surface: A football fixture at Manchester United's stadium, with a hint at a goalscorer in the penalty box.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford is also a Lancashire cricket ground used for Test matches, international games, so 'fixture' and 'striker' sound like football but aren't.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is an international cricket fixture, and Old Trafford in Manchester regularly hosts them.

clue.text: Desired outcome of 'Home, James!' is key

definitions.meaning: the order to a chauffeur aims to have the ... home
the key on a keyboard that starts a new line

explanation.definitionFit: Ordering a driver home seeks the coach's journey back; separately the typewriter key bearing that name starts a fresh line.

clue.text: Red top for breakfast type?

parts.note: ILK means type or kind, and MILK with its top skimmed off leaves ILK

explanation.surface: Choosing a tabloid newspaper to read over breakfast — a kind of person who does that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red top' suggests a British tabloid paper, but in the UK skimmed milk comes in red-capped bottles. Read as wordplay the answer says take the top off MILK, giving ILK, which is 'type'.
explanation.definitionFit: British milk bottles are colour-coded and the red cap marks the fat-free kind poured on cereal.

clue.text: Ask, maybe, but no-one will appreciate your doing it

definitions.text: no-one will appreciate your doing it

parts.note: TASK without TA (thanks) is ASK, so the answer read as wordplay is a, then task less thanks

explanation.surface: A grumble that making a request earns no gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal for thank you, so 'thankless TASK' read literally is TASK without TA, leaving ASK.
explanation.definitionFit: A job that earns no gratitude from anyone is the very meaning of an unrewarding chore.

clue.text: It produces nice glows in review, receiving Mark/Sherelle on vacation?

definitions.text: It produces nice glows in review, receiving Mark/Sherelle on vacation?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the pair from the next word
reviewing means going over again, here reworking these letters into a new order
emptied out, so only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A greeting placard cheering people up as they review it, featuring a name.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of NICE GLOWS gives WELCOSIGN, and 'receiving' puts ME (Mark/Sherelle with its inside emptied) into it. Read whole, the clue describes such a sign greeting returning holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting board for returning travellers produces warm feelings, shown by naming them on it.

clue.text: Hit the city: mischief for everyone!

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
a hob is a hobgoblin, a mischief-maker
each means every one, apiece

explanation.surface: An exhortation to go out on the town and cause trouble together.
explanation.walkthrough: Echo Beach is a 1980 hit single by the Canadian band Martha and the Muffins.
explanation.definitionFit: The song was a chart success, so it is a hit record by that new-wave group.

clue.text: See 11
Out of shape, suffering heart flutter?

indicators.note: a fluttering heart flips over, so the two letters at the centre of the word swap places

parts.note: form means shape

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of shape' looks like the definition, but only 'Out of' is; 'suffering heart flutter' makes the middle two letters of FORM swap.
explanation.definitionFit: From and out of both express origin or source, as in made from wood, out of wood.

clue.text: Fly vivace through A Harlot's Progress? That'll cause a splash!

indicators.note: the jumbled letters run through the middle of the other piece

parts.note: Iain Bell's 2013 opera, described as BELL OP, opera by Bell

indicators.note: vivace is the musical term for lively, so these letters are jiggled about

explanation.surface: A lively musical instruction for an opera, ending with a big splash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vivace' scrambles FLY to YFL, and 'through' places it inside BELL OP. OP is the standard abbreviation of opus or opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Landing flat on one's front when diving makes a large, painful splash in the pool.

clue.text: See 6
Characters in Alice rewritten to save new pop ballet

indicators.note: to keep safe within, so the shuffled name holds the other piece
written again in a different order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the name Alice

indicators.note: made new, so these three letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A modern pop retelling of Lewis Carroll's story with its characters reimagined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' scrambles the name and 'new' scrambles the three-letter word; 'to save' puts the second inside the first, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppélia is the 1870 comic ballet by Delibes about a life-sized dancing doll.

clue.text: One of the nibbles might do

parts.note: can, like might, expresses possibility
to do someone is to imitate them, to ape

explanation.surface: A suggestion at a party that one of the snacks would suffice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might do' reads as a single phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury snack served at drinks parties, one of the appetisers.

clue.text: Inspecting ____, start to uncover cracking fiddle in book

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: Acts is a book of the New Testament

indicators.note: breaking into the swindle, so the letter goes inside it

parts.note: a con is a swindle or fiddle

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: An auditor examining the books to expose a cracking fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the blank: with the answer filled in, the clue reads as auditing that exposes fiddled books, and the wordplay completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditors inspect financial records, so the missing word is the ledgers being examined.

clue.text: Could go quickly, this

parts.note: may and could both express possibility
to fly is to go quickly

explanation.surface: A remark that this thing might be gone in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an adult mayfly lives only a day or so, so it is gone quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult insect is notoriously short-lived, often surviving only hours, hence soon gone.

clue.text: Sweet tops?

parts.note: ice means kill (top) and cream means the best (tops), so two tops together make a frozen dessert

explanation.surface: A query whether a sweet is the very best.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words that each mean 'top' combine: ice is slang for kill, and the cream is the best.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a frozen dessert, and in Britain a sweet means a pudding course.

clue.text: Do very good seafood

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them, a scam
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: A recommendation to make some excellent seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustine tails, a popular seafood dish in Britain.

clue.text: Developer's very well informed

parts.note: so means very
to be up on something is to be well informed about it

explanation.surface: A property developer described as very knowledgeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developer' suggests property, but photographers call the developing chemical soup.
explanation.definitionFit: In darkroom slang, the chemical bath used to develop film is called soup.

clue.text: Cued by ringing, move writer

parts.note: to act is to move or take action
on followed by the word for a ringing instrument: prompted when it chimes

explanation.surface: Instructions to change position when a bell rings, like a school timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton Bell was the male pen name used by Anne Brontë.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Brontë published under this pseudonym, so it names a novelist.

clue.text: See 23
See 14
Current choice given to swing band

definitions.meaning: AC or DC, alternating or direct current
... is slang for bisexual, one who swings both ways

explanation.definitionFit: The pair of electrical current types, slang for bisexual, and the Australian rockers all share this name.

clue.text: Reform, say, before the bat in the bathroom?

definitions.meaning: the Reform is a London club that once admitted only men
a club (bat) in the gents (men's lavatory) is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: The Reform was a men-only London club until women were admitted, and a cudgel in the gents would be one.

clue.text: Zagreb: largest city in Croatia — and this instant!

definitions.text: Zagreb: largest city in Croatia — and this
definitions.meaning: Split is the second city of Croatia after Zagreb

explanation.definitionFit: Split ranks after the capital in size, and a fraction of a moment is an instant.
